captions: February 2012.
A developer clones an object with Apache Commons Lang, and it crashes.
The object only holds int dot class.
The report even includes the test that fails.
The maintainer can fix it.
But every maintainer also wants to know:
which change broke this, and when?
By then the project had more than three thousand commits.
Finding the culprit by hand means building old versions, one by one, and running a test on each.
So usually nobody does it, and the same kind of mistake comes back.
Bug Origin is a Rovo agent that lives in Jira.
When a bug is filed, an Automation rule wakes it up.
Nobody touches anything from here.
The agent reads the whole report, including who said what, and decides whether it is a bug at all.
Then it writes a small test that reproduces it, and runs it once on the reported version, to make sure the test really fails there.
If the test does not compile, the agent sees the error and the real API of that version, and fixes it.
It gets three tries, enforced in code.
A test that never failed is never trusted.
Then the runner on Google Cloud searches the history with that test.
Four old versions at a time, built and tested in parallel.
Pass, fail, pass.
Five rounds, twenty-two test runs, a hundred seconds.
The test passes on the commit before, and fails from this one on.
The answer:
a patch from August 2011, six months before the report.
It was itself a fix, for another user's class loading problem.
One fix quietly caused the next bug.
Now the team knows where it came from, and which kind of change to review harder.
We measured it before we believed it:
real Commons Lang bugs whose origins are known, and reports that are not bugs at all, fixed in advance.
The first run found the exact commit for six bugs out of eighteen.
We published every miss, fixed the causes, and ran again:
twelve out of eighteen.
When it was confident, it was right twelve times out of thirteen.
It abstained when it could not be sure, and fooled itself once, on a renamed method, which we now know how to catch.
Bug Origin.
File a bug, and get its origin, with the evidence attached.
Every number in this video links to the run that produced it.
